requirement: A job can carry a role briefing (video or audio) with transcript and chapters; Q answers questions from it, quoting the timestamp
Candidate can ask Q "can I contact someone about this role?"; Q answers what is known from the listing or policy first
Q shows the employer's contact policy before drafting (off, after applying, before applying; channels; limits) and proposes a concise relevant question
If direct contact is not enabled, Q offers the published application or contact route and never invents or scrapes a recruiter address
Candidate can edit the message, choose a permitted channel, and see statuses: draft, awaiting permission, approved, queued, sent, undelivered, seen (if known), replied, timeout, closed
Thread states also cover muted, reported, blocked, consent revoked and application withdrawn, each with what the candidate can still do
Replying in an established thread is allowed even when pre-application initiation is stricter, subject to the organisation's settings
Rate limits per candidate and organisation, anti-abuse (no mass unsolicited messages, no false identities), time zone and contact privacy are enforced
Recruiter side: candidate-initiated threads are marked as such, can be muted, reported or blocked, and routed to a role and campaign

Hierarchy: organisation → hiring campaign → requisition (role) → approved brief version and rubric → sourcing runs → applications → pipeline → interviews and correspondence → outcome and retrospective
A campaign groups roles for navigation and workload; it is not a second source of truth for roles or candidates (a role points to its campaign)
Agency extension: agency → client → client-specific campaigns and roles; shared candidate identity never implies cross-client visibility
Outreach campaigns stay separate: a child of a requisition or a client talent pool, not the same as a hiring campaign
Campaign overview: roles with stage counts, owners, deadlines, next actions, approvals waiting and messages by role
Cross-role board, saved filters, per-role scorecards, archive and re-open, audit, empty and conflict states
Q can create, name, organise, summarise and navigate campaigns in natural language, keeping context
Correspondence and candidate threads can be routed into a campaign and role by saying so; the link is audited

Q drafts job-related criteria from the approved brief, workplace guidelines and the job taxonomy (ESCO, D6): evidence to inspect, interview questions, practical methods, weights, minimum requirements and anchored levels 0-4
Recruiter edits or approves side by side with Q's proposal; approval creates an immutable version
Every candidate for the same role and stage is assessed against the same rubric version; ratings are bound to the version
Material mid-campaign changes require notice, audit and principled re-assessment; earlier ratings stay attached to their version
Signals stay separate: eligibility, demonstrated skills (with provenance), structured interview answers, practical assessments, candidate compatibility and availability, coverage and freshness
No criterion may select or proxy for protected characteristics; Q refuses and explains
Rubric revisions are listed with who, when, why and what changed
Weights, thresholds and job-relatedness are marked as needing research and empirical validation (not a validated test)
The comparison uses the approved rubric's weights for that role (replacing the fixed rule), with the weighting explained
Observed role-evidence index = 100·Σ(w·r/4)/Σw over observed criteria; coverage = 100·Σw(observed)/Σw(all); the index is never shown without coverage and the underlying evidence
evidence: qa/scripts/features/rubric.mjs; J11 steps 5, 8, 9; journeys/design/rubric.md; media report shows index with coverage

requirement: Unknown criteria are never scored as zero; the index is not a probability of performance, not global, and not comparable across roles
Uncertainty inspector: per criterion, which evidence, its freshness and reliability, and why the rating was given
Recruiter override needs a reason and is audited; consequential decisions require human review
Candidate explanation and appeal or correction route for ratings that affect them
Candidate adds a recorded project demo, mock interview or work presentation by upload, authorised link or portfolio link; employer-authorised interview recordings only with consent
Consent states scope (which organisations, which segments), purpose and expiry, before any processing
Ingest states: upload or link, fetching, transcribing, ready, failed fetch, unsafe link; uploads resume after interruption
Transcript review and correction by the candidate; key moments with timestamps; job-relevance marking
Visibility per item: private practice, shared with named employers, or public preview; segment-level sharing
Revoke and delete, subject to legal retention, with what the employer keeps stated
Text and form alternatives and an accommodation path are always offered
Never browse a candidate's unrelated media or use their credentials; only explicitly selected media is processed
Evidence report: every supported claim is timestamped and playable; findings map to rubric criteria with uncertainty
Prohibited inferences: no honesty, personality, emotion, confidence, accent, appearance, age, gender, race, disability or trustworthiness from face or voice
Spoken-communication criteria use task-related anchors with accessible alternatives; no accent or disability proxies
Recruiter human review state, disputed correction, and candidate self-review before sharing
Cost: transcribe once, cache by content hash and rubric version, visual frame review only when the task requires it, never re-run per page view
One persistent Q composer on every major experience; proactive notices grounded in live state; dismiss and snooze persist
evidence: One Q composer on every page (shell); dismiss/snooze persist (proactive engine); all journeys

requirement: A short film of the connected journey with simulation labels
Connect an email account: Google (Gmail and Workspace), Microsoft (Outlook, Microsoft 365, Outlook.com), other business email (SMTP/IMAP where supported); personal vs organisation account
Scope explanations before consent; send-only vs read-and-reply modes; minimum scopes per feature
Connection states: connected, verified, reconnection required (token expired), disconnected, revoked
Sender identity selector: personal, company, shared, agency and client addresses, each with its send permission; Talent Q platform notices use a separate verified service domain
Q resolves campaign, requisition, recipient identity, permitted address, sender, policy and template before drafting
Composer: editable To/Cc/Bcc, subject, body, attachments, tone, templates, signature, draft history; approve, send, schedule send
Pre-send checks: contact permission, rate limits, suppression, sender identity, external disclosure, attachment access
Approval covers the exact recipients and content; a material edit invalidates it; narrowly scoped delegation can pre-approve message classes
Truthful status model: draft, pending approval, approved, queued, accepted by provider, delivered only with provider evidence, bounced or failed, replied, cancelled; "sent" is not "received"
Correspondence lands in the candidate + role/campaign thread; follow-ups and reminders without duplication
With read access Q detects replies, summarises threads, extracts proposed times and unanswered questions; with send-only access it never claims to have read replies
Inbound messages map to sender, organisation, campaign, role and candidate; ambiguity goes to user review, never a silent attach
Email and attachments are untrusted content, not instructions; a reply cannot trigger actions or change permissions
"Stop contacting me" is recorded and enforced as suppression
A proposed time is checked against authorised calendars and policy; booked only when authorised; confirmation sent on the chosen channel
Proactive follow-up suggestions from thread state, with frequency caps, dismiss and snooze; pre-approved reminders only under explicit delegation; no unbounded mass email

Q recommends a channel (availability, preference, urgency, consent, deliverability); an authorised user can override; one conversation switches between email and in-app without losing context or duplicating the action
Correspondence hub: search; filter by organisation, client, campaign, requisition, candidate; unread, replied, awaiting reply; linked job context and next action
Reply intelligence: readable summary, quoted source, suggested response, extracted times, no fabricated commitments, approval where required
Multi-recipient review: individual drafts, per-recipient status, suppression and rate-limit marks, no exposure through To/Cc/Bcc
Attachments and Q artifacts (CVs, briefs, reports, invitations, consented evidence) shared under permission and expiry rules
Organisation email policy: templates, signatures, branding, language, legal notices, limits, channels, sending hours, delegated permissions, external-data policy, escalation

Errors and recovery: offline, SMTP rejected, OAuth expired, disconnected, read denied, unknown or malformed recipient, bounce, rate-limited, duplicate prevented, missing attachment, awaiting or revoked approval, suppressed recipient, manual resend
Audit and memory: what Q sent, why a person was contacted, which instructions applied, forget an extracted preference; a summary never replaces the canonical email record
R4: Q selects the correct authorised client sender and never leaks candidates across clients; a client's pre-approved reminder automation can be paused and Q obeys at once
R5: "send it from the CEO's Gmail" is refused; Q offers a draft for the authorised owner and explains the access needed
T1/T5: candidate inquiry by email from their connected mailbox only where the employer allows email contact; otherwise the published route
Consent change or withdrawal stops queued outreach and reminders; sent email cannot be unsent and the person is told so
A short communication clip (request → context → draft → approval → send status → reply → next action) on desktop and phone, watermarked as simulated
